You are Agent B of a code-quality audit on repo /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa, branch feature/SFCC-55_global-footer-ui.

YOUR SCOPE: **Import analysis only.** Do not audit naming, TypeScript typing, or test coverage.

Read .claude/rules/conventions.md ("Imports" section) and .claude/rules/overrideStyling.md (the section "Importing an already-overridden component from a new component") first. Also read .docs/memory/sprintScope.md if it exists.

For each file below, read its import statements and check:
1. **No circular imports** — if A imports B, read B's imports and confirm B does not import A.
2. **No imports from internal node_modules/@salesforce/... source paths** — must use published entrypoints.
3. **A component must not import data-fetching hooks** (@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react hooks, React Query) — per components.md "Container/presentational separation". Note: files under overrides/app/components/ receive data as props.
4. **No imports from a later-sprint feature** (cross-check .docs/memory/sprintScope.md).
5. **No `../../../..` chains longer than 3 levels.**
6. **THE BIG ONE — base-path vs relative import of an already-overridden component.** overrideStyling.md explains: if component A imports component B via '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/B' but B ALSO has an override in overrides/app/components/B/, then Storybook and Vitest silently render the BASE version, because the ccExtensibility resolver only runs in the real app build. For every base-path import of a component, check whether overrides/app/components/<that-name>/ exists. Report every hit.

3. For check 6, actually verify the override directory exists with `ls` before reporting. A base-path import of a component with NO local override is CORRECT and must not be flagged.

1	# Styling an Override Component
2	
3	How to style a component under `overrides/app/components/` or `overrides/app/theme/`.
4	Cross-references [overrides.md](./overrides.md) (module-replacement correctness — a
5	different concern: that file is about not breaking SFCC's own imports, this one is
6	about what values to reach for once the component compiles). Day-to-day CSS/token
7	rules live in [css.md](./css.md); this file is the practical "what do I actually type"
8	companion.
9	
10	---
11	
12	## The hierarchy — reach for these in order
13	
14	1. **`textStyle` prop** for anything textual. `textStyle="body2"`, never a raw `fontSize`.
15	   All 22 Handover text styles are registered in `theme/foundation/typography.ts`.
16	2. **Semantic colour/spacing token strings** — `color="text.default"`, `bg="background.02"`,
17	   `spacing="m"`, `padding={{ base: 'm', md: 'xl' }}`. These resolve through
18	   `theme.colors`/`theme.space` (both registered — see `theme/index.ts`'s own comment
19	   for which foundation scales are and aren't registered, and why).
20	3. **A component's own theme config** (`theme/components/<name>.ts`) for anything that
21	   needs to vary by variant/size/state and isn't already a Chakra prop — see
22	   "Component-local tokens" below. For an interactive component with existing Chakra
23	   support (buttons, inputs, etc.), this theme config is the single source of truth —
24	   see "One canonical styling surface per component type" below.
25	4. **`sx` prop** for a one-off Chakra-prop-system gap, per [css.md](./css.md).
26	5. **Scoped `.scss`** only when `sx` genuinely can't express it (complex pseudo-selectors,
27	   keyframes) — same file, same rules as [css.md](./css.md) already documents.
28	
29	**Never**: a raw hex/px/rem/em literal in a component file — reach for the token
30	instead. The one standing exception is `button.ts`'s provisional height/padding
31	constants (`BTN_HEIGHT_LG`/`BTN_HEIGHT_SM`/`BTN_PADDING_Y`), pending UI-designer
32	sign-off — see Units below. Run `node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` before opening
33	a PR that touches `overrides/app/components/**` or `overrides/app/theme/components/**`
34	— it greps for exactly this. It is not wired into CI yet — that's a reasonable next
35	step once someone owns triaging its false positives (hairline px is expected and
36	not a bug; see below).
37	
38	## Units
39	
40	- **`rem`** for anything that should scale with the user's root font-size / browser zoom
41	  (WCAG 1.4.4): type (`fontSize`, `lineHeight`, `letterSpacing`) and spacing
42	  (`spacing.ts`'s named scale). Letter-spacing values that were specified as sub-pixel px
43	  in the source don't round to clean rem numbers, so those keep a trailing `// -0.12px`
44	  comment for traceability.
45	- **`px`** for hairline geometry that should _not_ scale: border widths, focus-ring
46	  offsets, and (for now) the provisional button-height constants in `button.ts` that are
47	  still pending UI-designer sign-off against Handover.
48	- **`em`** only for breakpoints (`gridSystem.ts` — deliberate, so `.zimm-grid`'s media
49	  queries shift with zoom the same way Chakra's responsive props do) and other
50	  genuinely context-relative cases. Not a general-purpose unit.
51	
52	## The alias tier is a reference, not a second copy
53	
54	`theme/foundation/colour.ts`'s primitive tier (`grey`, `ivory`, ...) is defined first as
55	plain `const`s, and the semantic/alias tier below it (`text`, `background`, `border`,
56	...) reads from those consts (`text.default: grey[900]`) instead of retyping the hex
57	value. Do the same for any new primitive/alias pair you add — two values can't disagree
58	if only one of them is ever typed.
59	
60	`zimmTokens.ts` (the `--zimm-*` CSS-var registry for `globalStyles.ts`'s `.zimm-*`
61	classes) is fully derived the same way — it imports `colors`/`spacing`/`fontSizes`/
62	`lineHeights`/`letterSpacings`/`fontWeights`/`iconSizes`/`actionSizes`/`motion`/`grid`
63	from their owning files rather than retyping values. The only literals left are the 7
64	numeric `--zimm-scale-NNN` aliases with no named-scale equivalent (`025`, `700`, `1100`,
65	`1200`, `1300`, `3500`, `4500`) — not duplicates, just Handover values with nothing to
66	derive them from. `theme/index.test.tsx`'s collision-guard tests still exist as a
67	regression net; treat a failure there as a real drift signal, not test noise.
68	
69	## One canonical styling surface per component type
70	
71	Only one place should define how a given interactive component looks: its
72	`theme/components/<name>.ts` config, consumed via Chakra's component (`<Button>`,
73	`<Link>` variant, etc.). Don't also give it a `.zimm-*` global class in
74	`globalStyles.ts` — a static CSS class can't express `_hover`/`_active`/`_disabled`/
75	`_focusVisible` states the way a Chakra theme config can, so a class "mirror" is
76	structurally incomplete from the start, and nothing stops its values from disagreeing
77	with the real theme config over time. `button.ts` is the single source of truth for
78	button styling; `globalStyles.ts` has no `.zimm-btn-*` classes — use Chakra's `<Button>`
79	for any button, not a class.
80	
81	`.zimm-*` classes remain the right tool for genuinely static, non-interactive,
82	massively-reused treatments (typography, the responsive grid, form-field layout) where
83	there's no interactive state to lose.
84	
85	## Importing an already-overridden component from a new component
86	
87	If component A (e.g. `productDetailOptions`) uses component B, and B already has an
88	override (e.g. `swatch-group`), **import B via a relative path
89	(`'../swatch-group'`), not the SFCC base path
90	(`'@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/swatch-group'`)** — even though the
91	base path is exactly what [overrides.md](./overrides.md) requires _inside_ an override
92	that's itself shadowing an SFCC module (see `product-tile/index.tsx`'s `DisplayPrice`
93	import, which is correct for that file).
94	
95	The reason the two cases differ: the resolver that redirects
96	`@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` imports to `overrides/` (`ccExtensibility` in
97	`package.json`, read by a webpack plugin) only runs in the **real app build** — dev
98	server and production. `.storybook/main.js` aliases that package straight to
99	`node_modules` and `vitest.config.ts` doesn't touch it at all, so neither loads the
100	resolver. A base-path import of an already-overridden component will build and run
101	correctly in the shipped app, but silently render/test the **unstyled base SFCC
102	version** in Storybook and Vitest — the story or test looks like it's exercising your
103	override and isn't.
104	
105	**Known instance of this, not yet fixed:** `product-tile/index.tsx`'s `DisplayPrice`
106	import uses the base path. Currently dormant only because its Storybook story exercises
107	the `CardBaseline` named export (which takes `price` as a pre-rendered node and never
108	calls `DisplayPrice`), not the default `ProductTile` bridge that actually renders it —
109	worth fixing before anything writes a story/test against the default export.
110	
111	An override component's own base-path imports (of modules it is _not_ also
112	overriding) are unaffected by this — `RecommendedProducts`, `Seo`, `QuantityPicker`
113	etc. have no local override to miss, so the base path is simply correct for them.
114	
115	## Component-local tokens
116	
117	When a component needs a spacing/sizing value that already has a `spacing.ts` /
118	`iconSizes` / etc. entry, reference it **by name** in the theme config
119	(`marginBottom: 'xs'`, not `marginBottom: 2` or `marginBottom: '0.5rem'`) — Chakra
120	resolves named scale keys against the registered `theme.space` automatically. See
121	`theme/components/imageGallery.ts` / `swatchGroup.ts` for the pattern: both re-express
122	values the base SFCC theme already had as anonymous Chakra numerics (`marginBottom: 2`)
123	using our named scale instead, at the same responsive steps (`['2xs', '2xs', 'xs',
124	'xs']` instead of `[1, 1, 2, 2]`) — same computed output, now traceable to a brand
125	token.
126	
127	When a component needs a dimension with **no existing foundation entry** (and you don't
128	have a confirmed Figma value for it), leave it inherited from the base SFCC theme rather
129	than inventing a number — don't guess at design values. Follow the precedent already in
130	`header.ts`/`button.ts`: if you do have to ship a placeholder value pending designer
131	sign-off, say so in a comment next to it, the same way those files already do.
132	
133	## The SFCC bridge pattern (shared components only)
134	
135	If the component is used internally by SFCC's own base components (check with `grep -r
136	"from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/<name>'"
137	node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/`), its **default export must stay a
138	faithful, undecorated port** — full original prop surface, same `forwardRef` behaviour,
139	matching what [overrides.md](./overrides.md) already requires for correctness. Put
140	Zimmermann-only styling behind a **named export** that wraps the default and adds
141	brand-specific defaults, the same split `product-tile/index.tsx` (`CardBaseline`
142	name + default) and `link/index.tsx` already use. `image-gallery`, `display-price`, and
143	`swatch-group` are all shared internal SFCC dependencies — their default exports are
144	kept API-compatible; brand styling for them lives in their `theme/components/*.ts`
145	config instead of a named-export split, since token-driven theming doesn't require a
146	second export the way `CardBaseline`'s prop-narrowing did.
147	
148	---
149	
150	## Known gaps (not silently dropped — logged here)
151	
152	- The f2r `zimm-product-detail-options` prototype spec includes a size-as-dropdown
153	  picker, a wishlist button, a "find in boutique" link, and description/shipping
154	  accordions. None of those exist as overrides yet, so `ProductDetailOptions` ships
155	  without them — it's colour/size swatches, quantity, and add-to-bag only.
156	- `swatch-group`'s `square`/`circle` variant functions (selected/disabled colour logic,
157	  the diagonal disabled-state gradient) are still inherited from the base SFCC theme —
158	  real visual design decisions with no Zimmermann Figma spec behind them yet.
159	- `button.ts`'s `BTN_HEIGHT_LG`/`BTN_HEIGHT_SM` (50px/41px) disagree with the
160	  Handover-sourced `actionSizes.height.lg`/`.md` (52px/40px) — flagged in `button.ts`,
161	  pending UI-designer sign-off. `BTN_PADDING_Y` (5px) has no Handover token at all —
162	  a gap to fill, not a conflict to resolve.
163	- `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/` is claimed by `.claude/rules/squadA.md`
164	  (draft, scope still settling) — flagged for awareness, not treated as a hard block.
165	
166	## Follow-up work (separate initiatives)
167	
168	- **Per-component CSS loading.** `globalStyles.ts`'s `.zimm-*` class registry is

# Styling an Override Component

How to style a component under `overrides/app/components/` or `overrides/app/theme/`.
Cross-references [overrides.md](./overrides.md) (module-replacement correctness — a
different concern: that file is about not breaking SFCC's own imports, this one is
about what values to reach for once the component compiles). Day-to-day CSS/token
rules live in [css.md](./css.md); this file is the practical "what do I actually type"
companion.

---

## The hierarchy — reach for these in order

1. **`textStyle` prop** for anything textual. `textStyle="body2"`, never a raw `fontSize`.
   All 22 Handover text styles are registered in `theme/foundation/typography.ts`.
2. **Semantic colour/spacing token strings** — `color="text.default"`, `bg="background.02"`,
   `spacing="m"`, `padding={{ base: 'm', md: 'xl' }}`. These resolve through
   `theme.colors`/`theme.space` (both registered — see `theme/index.ts`'s own comment
   for which foundation scales are and aren't registered, and why).
3. **A component's own theme config** (`theme/components/<name>.ts`) for anything that
   needs to vary by variant/size/state and isn't already a Chakra prop — see
   "Component-local tokens" below. For an interactive component with existing Chakra
   support (buttons, inputs, etc.), this theme config is the single source of truth —
   see "One canonical styling surface per component type" below.
4. **`sx` prop** for a one-off Chakra-prop-system gap, per [css.md](./css.md).
5. **Scoped `.scss`** only when `sx` genuinely can't express it (complex pseudo-selectors,
   keyframes) — same file, same rules as [css.md](./css.md) already documents.

**Never**: a raw hex/px/rem/em literal in a component file — reach for the token
instead. The one standing exception is `button.ts`'s provisional height/padding
constants (`BTN_HEIGHT_LG`/`BTN_HEIGHT_SM`/`BTN_PADDING_Y`), pending UI-designer
sign-off — see Units below. Run `node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` before opening
a PR that touches `overrides/app/components/**` or `overrides/app/theme/components/**`
— it greps for exactly this. It is not wired into CI yet — that's a reasonable next
step once someone owns triaging its false positives (hairline px is expected and
not a bug; see below).

## Units

- **`rem`** for anything that should scale with the user's root font-size / browser zoom
  (WCAG 1.4.4): type (`fontSize`, `lineHeight`, `letterSpacing`) and spacing
  (`spacing.ts`'s named scale). Letter-spacing values that were specified as sub-pixel px
  in the source don't round to clean rem numbers, so those keep a trailing `// -0.12px`
  comment for traceability.
- **`px`** for hairline geometry that should _not_ scale: border widths, focus-ring
  offsets, and (for now) the provisional button-height constants in `button.ts` that are
  still pending UI-designer sign-off against Handover.
- **`em`** only for breakpoints (`gridSystem.ts` — deliberate, so `.zimm-grid`'s media
  queries shift with zoom the same way Chakra's responsive props do) and other
  genuinely context-relative cases. Not a general-purpose unit.

## The alias tier is a reference, not a second copy

`theme/foundation/colour.ts`'s primitive tier (`grey`, `ivory`, ...) is defined first as
plain `const`s, and the semantic/alias tier below it (`text`, `background`, `border`,
...) reads from those consts (`text.default: grey[900]`) instead of retyping the hex
value. Do the same for any new primitive/alias pair you add — two values can't disagree
if only one of them is ever typed.

`zimmTokens.ts` (the `--zimm-*` CSS-var registry for `globalStyles.ts`'s `.zimm-*`
classes) is fully derived the same way — it imports `colors`/`spacing`/`fontSizes`/
`lineHeights`/`letterSpacings`/`fontWeights`/`iconSizes`/`actionSizes`/`motion`/`grid`
from their owning files rather than retyping values. The only literals left are the 7
numeric `--zimm-scale-NNN` aliases with no named-scale equivalent (`025`, `700`, `1100`,
`1200`, `1300`, `3500`, `4500`) — not duplicates, just Handover values with nothing to
derive them from. `theme/index.test.tsx`'s collision-guard tests still exist as a
regression net; treat a failure there as a real drift signal, not test noise.

## One canonical styling surface per component type

Only one place should define how a given interactive component looks: its
`theme/components/<name>.ts` config, consumed via Chakra's component (`<Button>`,
`<Link>` variant, etc.). Don't also give it a `.zimm-*` global class in
`globalStyles.ts` — a static CSS class can't express `_hover`/`_active`/`_disabled`/
`_focusVisible` states the way a Chakra theme config can, so a class "mirror" is
structurally incomplete from the start, and nothing stops its values from disagreeing
with the real theme config over time. `button.ts` is the single source of truth for
button styling; `globalStyles.ts` has no `.zimm-btn-*` classes — use Chakra's `<Button>`
for any button, not a class.

`.zimm-*` classes remain the right tool for genuinely static, non-interactive,
massively-reused treatments (typography, the responsive grid, form-field layout) where
there's no interactive state to lose.

## Importing an already-overridden component from a new component

If component A (e.g. `productDetailOptions`) uses component B, and B already has an
override (e.g. `swatch-group`), **import B via a relative path
(`'../swatch-group'`), not the SFCC base path
(`'@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/swatch-group'`)** — even though the
base path is exactly what [overrides.md](./overrides.md) requires _inside_ an override
that's itself shadowing an SFCC module (see `product-tile/index.tsx`'s `DisplayPrice`
import, which is correct for that file).

The reason the two cases differ: the resolver that redirects
`@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` imports to `overrides/` (`ccExtensibility` in
`package.json`, read by a webpack plugin) only runs in the **real app build** — dev
server and production. `.storybook/main.js` aliases that package straight to
`node_modules` and `vitest.config.ts` doesn't touch it at all, so neither loads the
resolver. A base-path import of an already-overridden component will build and run
correctly in the shipped app, but silently render/test the **unstyled base SFCC
version** in Storybook and Vitest — the story or test looks like it's exercising your
override and isn't.

**Known instance of this, not yet fixed:** `product-tile/index.tsx`'s `DisplayPrice`
import uses the base path. Currently dormant only because its Storybook story exercises
the `CardBaseline` named export (which takes `price` as a pre-rendered node and never
calls `DisplayPrice`), not the default `ProductTile` bridge that actually renders it —
worth fixing before anything writes a story/test against the default export.

An override component's own base-path imports (of modules it is _not_ also
overriding) are unaffected by this — `RecommendedProducts`, `Seo`, `QuantityPicker`
etc. have no local override to miss, so the base path is simply correct for them.

## Component-local tokens

When a component needs a spacing/sizing value that already has a `spacing.ts` /
`iconSizes` / etc. entry, reference it **by name** in the theme config
(`marginBottom: 'xs'`, not `marginBottom: 2` or `marginBottom: '0.5rem'`) — Chakra
resolves named scale keys against the registered `theme.space` automatically. See
`theme/components/imageGallery.ts` / `swatchGroup.ts` for the pattern: both re-express
values the base SFCC theme already had as anonymous Chakra numerics (`marginBottom: 2`)
using our named scale instead, at the same responsive steps (`['2xs', '2xs', 'xs',
'xs']` instead of `[1, 1, 2, 2]`) — same computed output, now traceable to a brand
token.

When a component needs a dimension with **no existing foundation entry** (and you don't
have a confirmed Figma value for it), leave it inherited from the base SFCC theme rather
than inventing a number — don't guess at design values. Follow the precedent already in
`header.ts`/`button.ts`: if you do have to ship a placeholder value pending designer
sign-off, say so in a comment next to it, the same way those files already do.

## The SFCC bridge pattern (shared components only)

If the component is used internally by SFCC's own base components (check with `grep -r
"from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/<name>'"
node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/`), its **default export must stay a
faithful, undecorated port** — full original prop surface, same `forwardRef` behaviour,
matching what [overrides.md](./overrides.md) already requires for correctness. Put
Zimmermann-only styling behind a **named export** that wraps the default and adds
brand-specific defaults, the same split `product-tile/index.tsx` (`CardBaseline`
name + default) and `link/index.tsx` already use. `image-gallery`, `display-price`, and
`swatch-group` are all shared internal SFCC dependencies — their default exports are
kept API-compatible; brand styling for them lives in their `theme/components/*.ts`
config instead of a named-export split, since token-driven theming doesn't require a
second export the way `CardBaseline`'s prop-narrowing did.

---

## Known gaps (not silently dropped — logged here)

- The f2r `zimm-product-detail-options` prototype spec includes a size-as-dropdown
  picker, a wishlist button, a "find in boutique" link, and description/shipping
  accordions. None of those exist as overrides yet, so `ProductDetailOptions` ships
  without them — it's colour/size swatches, quantity, and add-to-bag only.
- `swatch-group`'s `square`/`circle` variant functions (selected/disabled colour logic,
  the diagonal disabled-state gradient) are still inherited from the base SFCC theme —
  real visual design decisions with no Zimmermann Figma spec behind them yet.
- `button.ts`'s `BTN_HEIGHT_LG`/`BTN_HEIGHT_SM` (50px/41px) disagree with the
  Handover-sourced `actionSizes.height.lg`/`.md` (52px/40px) — flagged in `button.ts`,
  pending UI-designer sign-off. `BTN_PADDING_Y` (5px) has no Handover token at all —
  a gap to fill, not a conflict to resolve.
- `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/` is claimed by `.claude/rules/squadA.md`
  (draft, scope still settling) — flagged for awareness, not treated as a hard block.

## Follow-up work (separate initiatives)

- **Per-component CSS loading.** `globalStyles.ts`'s `.zimm-*` class registry is
  registered as one `theme.styles.global` block and ships on every page regardless of
  which classes a given page's components actually use. If component overrides start
  applying `.zimm-*` classNames directly for the non-interactive cases described above,
  only the classes a page's components actually reference should load, not the whole
  registry. Needs its own investigation, not scoped or estimated yet.
- **`globalStyles.ts` adoption is currently near zero.** Of the classes still defined
  there, none have a real consumer anywhere in the app today except one Storybook demo
  (`spacing.stories.tsx`'s `.zimm-grid` example). They're Handover-ported 1:1 and
  presumably _intended_ to be reused, just not adopted by any component yet — worth
  revisiting once component overrides actually start applying them.

Import analysis complete. All checks run mechanically and verified against the filesystem.

## MUST-FIX

**1. `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx:40-51` — base-path icons import shadows an existing override, and *this branch* is what made the two diverge.**

```
import { AccountIcon, BasketIcon, BrandLogo, HamburgerIcon, ChevronDownIcon,
         HeartIcon, SearchIcon, SignoutIcon, StoreIcon, SparkleIcon
} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/icons';   // ← line 51
```

- Override confirmed to exist: `overrides/app/components/icons/index.tsx`.
- **The import line itself is PRE-EXISTING** (`git diff origin/develop` on this file shows only surrounding comments added).
- **The divergence is NEW on this branch.** `overrides/app/components/icons/index.tsx:19-22` was changed here to *stop* re-exporting `ChevronDownIcon`/`Left`/`Right`/`Up` from the base template — they now come from `overrides/app/components/icons/zimm.tsx:102-124`. Before this branch, base and override agreed on `ChevronDownIcon`; they no longer do. `header/index.tsx:277` actually renders `<ChevronDownIcon />`.
- Effect per overrideStyling.md: real app build resolves to the override (stroked Zimmermann chevron); Storybook (`.storybook/main.js:31` aliases `@salesforce/retail-react-app` → `node_modules`) and Vitest (`vitest.config.ts` has no such alias at all) resolve to base. Worse than a style mismatch — base icons are sprite-based (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/icons/index.jsx:17-60`) and `.storybook/main.js:53-57` routes SFCC `.svg` to `ignore-loader`, so a Storybook render would show **no glyph**.
- Also a direct violation of AGENTS.md > Rules > **Icons** ("Do not import from `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/icons` directly").
- **Currently dormant**: `overrides/app/components/header/` contains only `index.tsx` — no story, no test, and no `.stories.tsx`/`.test.ts*` anywhere references `components/header`. Same shape as the documented `product-tile`/`DisplayPrice` case.
- Fix is one token: `from 'app/components/icons'` — the alias the new `zimmIcon` atom already uses correctly (`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmIcon/index.tsx:41`). Caveat: `header/` is Tier 2 Global Shell (both squads) per protectedFiles.md, so coordinate or log it rather than fixing silently on a footer branch.

## SHOULD-FIX

**2. `overrides/app/components/footer/index.tsx:14` — `import { HOME_HREF } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/constants'`. NEW on this branch.** `overrides/app/constants/index.ts` exists, so this is the same check-6 pattern. No functional divergence *today* — that override ends with `export * from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/constants'` (line 17), so every base constant has an identical value in both resolvers. Still worth switching to `app/constants` while it's new code, since it costs nothing and removes the trap.

## BACKLOG

**3. Pre-existing siblings of finding 2** (same reasoning, same dormancy, not this PR's code): `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx:59` (`STORE_LOCATOR_IS_ENABLED`) and `overrides/app/components/_app-config/index.tsx:44`. The latent risk across all three: the day someone *changes* rather than *adds* a value in `overrides/app/constants/index.ts` (which today holds only the additive `CUSTOM_HOME_TITLE`, line 8), Storybook/Vitest silently keep the base value with no signal.

**4. `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx:26` and `:28` — data-fetching hooks in a component**, violating components.md container/presentational separation: `AuthHelpers, useAuthHelper, useCustomerType` from `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`, and `useCurrentBasket`. Both **PRE-EXISTING** and untouched by this branch — inherent to the copied base SFCC header (file's own line 1 says "This component was a draft, unfinished"). Not introduced here.

## Verified clean (stating explicitly so these aren't re-flagged)

- **Circular imports: zero.** Mechanically verified across the entire `overrides/**` graph plus `.storybook/preview.tsx`, resolving relative, `app/`, and `~/` specifiers with comments stripped. No cycles anywhere, including footer ↔ `contentfulFixture`, atoms ↔ molecules, and `theme/components` ↔ `theme/foundation`.
- **Internal `node_modules/...` imports: none.** `@salesforce/pwa-kit-runtime/utils/ssr-namespace-paths` (`overrides/app/theme/fontFace.tsx:3`, `_app-config/index.tsx:24`) is the package's documented published subpath — that package ships no `exports` map and the module's own JSDoc prescribes that path.
- **Deep relative chains: none in scope.** Deepest in the audited set is 2 levels (`zimmInputAction/index.tsx:3-5`, `_app-config/index.tsx:9-15`). The only 3-level chains in the repo are in `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/` — out of scope, pre-existing, and exactly at the limit rather than over it.
- **Later-sprint imports: none.** The only adjacent symbol is `StoreLocatorProvider` (`_app-config/index.tsx:16`; Store Locator is Sprint 5/Squad B) — upstream SFCC template code, pre-existing, untouched by this diff. Contentful use in the footer is explicitly permitted by `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md`.
- **The two remaining `OVERRIDE-EXISTS` base-path imports are correct self-shadowing bridges**, not findings: `overrides/app/components/icons/index.tsx:73` and `overrides/app/theme/index.ts:15`. The `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/footer` string at `overrides/app/components/footer/index.tsx:557` is inside a JSDoc comment, not an import.
- **Every other base-path import has no local override** (checked against the filesystem): `components/link`, `loading-spinner`, `responsive`, `search`, `shared/ui`, `with-registration`, `contexts`, `hooks/use-current-basket`, `hooks/use-multi-site`, `hooks/use-navigation`, `pages/account/constant`, `utils/{auth,config,site,url,utils,sfdc-user-agent}`. Note `overrides/app/hooks/` contains only `useContentful*`, `useCountryConfig*`, `useZimmTextInputState*` — none of the kebab-case SFCC hook overrides listed in frozenFiles.md exist yet, so base-path is correct for them today.
- **`app/...` alias imports are safe in all four resolvers** — verified `babel.config.js:24`, `tsconfig.json:11`, `.storybook/main.js:30`, `vitest.config.ts` alias block all map `app` → `overrides/app`. The new footer/ui-kits code uses this consistently and thereby sidesteps the check-6 trap entirely.
- **Footer respects container/presentational separation.** The presentational `Footer` (`overrides/app/components/footer/index.tsx:435`) takes `data: FooterConfigEntry` as a prop and calls only Chakra/React hooks; `FooterContainer` (`:566`) calls `useMultiSite()` and `useHistory()`, neither of which fetches (base `use-multi-site.js` is a pure `useContext(MultiSiteContext)` read). No `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` or React Query import exists anywhere under `overrides/app/components/` except header. The container's own JSDoc (`:560-563`) pre-flags the components.md tension for the future HPC-034 Contentful fetch — self-documented, correctly deferred.
- Files with zero imports, nothing to flag: `overrides/app/utils/safeHref.ts`, `overrides/app/types/contentful.ts`, `overrides/app/components/footer/contentfulSchema.placeholder.ts`, `theme/components/{button,zimmNavItem,zimmTextInput}.ts` (Chakra only).

One informational aside (not an import-rule violation): `overrides/app/components/footer/contentfulSchema.placeholder.ts` is imported by nothing repo-wide — likely an intentional spec artifact for HPC-034, but worth a confirmation from the author.
